title: Cua Driver Bench on AgentEnv

gallery.title: Takes the user's keyboard focus
gallery.caption: Setting Priority opens BenchLab's pop-up menu, which takes the keyboard from the person typing and leaves BenchLab on top of their window. The task is done; the trial fails.

gallery.title: Raises its app over the user's window
gallery.caption: It sets Quantity and clicks the Priority menu open: BenchLab comes up over the user's window, the open menu holds the keyboard, and the user's next seven keystrokes are lost.

gallery.title: A clean pass: the user never notices
gallery.caption: The same task and seed through cua-driver: it sets both fields and presses Apply while BenchLab stays behind the user's window. No focus taken, no window raised, every keystroke lands.

gallery.title: A modal dialog takes the user's keyboard
gallery.caption: Once the email is in, BenchLab opens its cookie-consent dialog. Linux's window manager stacks a modal dialog over every window and hands it the keyboard, so every keystroke the user types after it is lost, whatever the agent does.

gallery.title: Every click refused, so it gives up
gallery.caption: On Linux cua-driver can't send clicks or keys to a covered Electron, Chromium or Calc window. Each try at the mail app is refused, so the agent replies BLOCKED: the user is never disturbed, and the task is never done.

gallery.title: Tries a shell through launch_app
gallery.caption: It can't open a log file through the apps, so it asks cua-driver's launch_app to run sh -c 'cp …'. A shell is a way out of the GUI, so the trial fails GUI-only whether or not the command ran.

gallery.title: Runs out of turns mid-task
gallery.caption: It is still working through the calendar when it takes its 45th turn and the harness stops it, the schedule unfinished. All 15 of Sonnet's multi-app foreground trials through agent-desktop end at the turn limit.

gallery.title: Has no hover, so the tooltip never shows
gallery.caption: browser-use's harness has no command that just points. To show the Cube icon's tooltip the agent clicks, holds, drags and scrolls on it; the tooltip never appears, and it replies BLOCKED. Through browser-use, Sonnet and Haiku fail all 20 hover trials (MB-10 and MB-11); through cua-driver and agent-desktop they pass every one.

gallery.name: dialog-windows
gallery.title: On Windows too, a modal dialog takes the user's keyboard
gallery.caption: After the form's first step BenchLab opens a permission dialog, and Windows gives it the keyboard: the user's window loses focus and the keystrokes they type next are blocked. The agent denies the permission and submits the form, so the task is done and the trial fails.

gallery.name: turns-windows
gallery.title: Runs out of turns on Windows
gallery.caption: It has fixed the calendar and recorded the blocker, and is reading the workbook's Controls sheet when it takes its 45th turn, so the schedule rows stay tentative. 23 of the 30 multi-app trials on Windows end on the turn limit.

caveats.reason: The interruption is a modal dialog. On Linux the window manager stacks it over the user's window (xfwm4 also gives it the keyboard; openbox, trycua's Linux choice, only stacks it), so the user is disturbed whatever the agent does. On macOS a background app's sheet stays behind.
A real drag moves the user's pointer, so in the background the task keeps the user undisturbed only through a driver that drags without it.

caveats.short: A dialog takes the keyboard on Windows
caveats.reason: The interruption is a modal dialog. When it opens, Windows usually gives it the keyboard and activates it, so the user's window loses focus and the keystrokes they type next are blocked.

driver_why.title: Why cua-driver beats Codex Computer Use on macOS
driver_why.lead: Claude Sonnet 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Sol each ran every trial through both drivers, 360 trials in all. In the background cua-driver passes 23 and 16 of 40, Codex Computer Use 11 and 8; in the foreground cua-driver passes 39 and 30 of 50, Codex Computer Use 26 and 28. Each reason below is read from the trials' tool calls, the drivers' own replies and the sentinel's record of the user's screen.

points.head: cua-driver acts on an app without bringing it forward.
points.text: Its background clicks are accessibility presses (`AXPress`), its text goes into a field's `AXValue`, it picks a pop-up's item through accessibility without opening the menu, and it sends keys to the app's own process. It disturbed the user in 4 of Sonnet's 40 background trials and 10 of GPT's.

points.head: Codex Computer Use's click on a pop-up menu brings the app forward.
points.text: Before a trial's first raise, 8 of Codex's 10 clicks on a pop-up button raised the app over the user's window, against 8 of its 62 clicks on plain buttons; cua-driver's 29 calls on a pop-up raised it in 3. IR-01's Team and IR-02's Priority are pop-ups, so each model passes 1 of 5 background trials of each through Codex, and 4 of 5 through cua-driver.

points.head: In the multi-app tasks, Codex's first click in an app brings that app over the user's window.
points.text: Every background trial in which Codex clicked one of the task's apps (mail, chat, calendar, cases, the manual or LibreOffice) raised it but one: Sonnet's 15 of 15 and GPT's 12 of 13, and none passed. cua-driver presses the same apps' buttons through accessibility, and Sonnet passes G04 in the background 4 of 5, GPT 2 of 5.

points.head: Neither driver can drag in the background, for different reasons.
points.text: Codex's drag activates BenchLab: it raised the window in 3 of Sonnet's 5 MB-09 background trials, and GPT saw the activation and stopped in 4 of 5. cua-driver releases a background drag that starts a macOS drag-and-drop session, as reordering a list does, and both models stop: none of its 10 pass.

points.head: Codex's own window sits over the user's too, but never alone.
points.text: The “ChatGPT Computer Use” window was above the user's in 25 of Codex's 80 background trials, each of them one in which Codex had also raised a task app's window, so it fails no trial by itself.

points.head: Codex Computer Use has no hover.
points.text: MB-10's toolbar and MB-11's tooltip show only under the pointer, so all 20 of their foreground trials through Codex end with the agent reporting itself blocked. Through cua-driver Sonnet moves the pointer (`move_cursor`), reads the screenshot and passes all 10.

points.head: GPT works on cua-driver without seeing the screen.
points.text: Codex CLI hands GPT cua-driver's structured results without their screenshots, and BenchLab's hover toolbar and tooltip and GnuCash's register aren't in the accessibility tree, so GPT stops in all 15 of MB-10's, MB-11's and G03's foreground trials and says why. In IR-04's background it can't check that its typing landed, so in 4 of 5 it writes the email to the user's clipboard and pastes it; Sonnet checks the screenshot and passes all 5. Codex Computer Use's results carry no structured content, so through it GPT does see the screen.

points.head: cua-driver tells GPT that LibreOffice can't be edited in the background, and GPT believes it.
points.text: In G02's background cua-driver answers a cell write with “LibreOffice ignores accessibility value writes and drops background pointer input, so its cells cannot be edited in the background”. GPT stops in 4 of 5 and pastes the rows through the user's clipboard in the fifth. Sonnet gets the same answer and passes one by moving and typing in Calc with keys sent to LibreOffice's process.

points.head: GPT presses Apply before Codex's menu choice lands.
points.text: In IR-02's foreground GPT picks the Priority item and presses Apply in one `js` call; in 4 of 5 BenchLab records the Apply with the old priority, and the field shows the new one only after. Through cua-driver, `set_value` sets the priority before GPT presses Apply, and it passes all 5.
